answer_1.quote: Our goal in this paper is to fill this gap and provide a comprehensive evaluation of instruction-tuned models prompted to generate English disinformation "news articles".

answer_2.quote: We compared the answers generated by GPT-4 with human annotators.

answer_3.quote: We evaluate the feasibility of using LLMs (GPT-4 in our case) to rate generated texts and automate the assessment process.
methods: separate request for each generated text and question mimicking the rating done by humans
prompt contains narrative title and abstract, generated text, and one of the 6 evaluation questions with possible answers

answer_4.quote: For this experiment, human annotators were used to rate 840 texts generated by 7 LLMs.
answer_4.guideline: The first two questions pertain to the form of the generated text. Q1 measures whether the text is coherent, while Q2 focuses on the style, i.e., whether the text "looks like" a news article. Q3 and Q4 are about the stance of the text towards the narrative -does the text support it and agree with it, or does it actively disprove it. Finally, Q5 and Q6 are measures of how many arguments for and against the narrative were generated by the LLM.
